page: Microsoft Azure E64bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine within the Ebsv6 series, powered by dedicated Intel x86_64 processors. Designed for memory-intensive enterprise workloads, it provides 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of system memory, establishing a 1:8 core-to-memory ratio with 8 GB of RAM allocated per vCPU. Virtualization is managed via Microsoft Hyper-V, and the instance operates without hardware graphics accelerators.

Unlike instance variants with integrated ephemeral disks, the E64bs_v6 includes no local storage. Instead, the architecture is engineered for high-performance remote block storage, supporting Azure Premium Storage to fulfill data-tier IO requirements. Network configuration allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, necessitating configured networking resources or gateways for external connectivity.

From a resource allocation perspective, the server offers high density for memory and compute without incurring the hardware overhead of dedicated local NVMe drives or GPUs. This profile suits large-scale production environments where state is decoupled from compute, making the E64bs_v6 appropriate for enterprise relational databases, large in-memory data analytics, distributed caching systems, and batch ETL processing pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E64bs_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on Microsoft Hyper-V with an x86_64 Intel processor architecture. Configured with 64 dedicated vCPUs and 512 GB of RAM, the instance delivers an 8 GB per vCPU allocation designed for large memory footprints. The system features no onboard local storage, instead relying on decoupled, high-performance remote block storage architectures with Premium Storage compatibility. There are no bundled GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By prioritizing a dense 1:8 compute-to-memory profile without the overhead of physical accelerator hardware or integrated local drives, the instance provides qualitative resource efficiency for decoupled infrastructure designs. It is suited for enterprise relational database engines, massive distributed in-memory caches, data warehouse workloads, and memory-bound ETL pipelines requiring dedicated vCPU performance.
